'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[2022 Ukrainian summer counteroffensive]]
****[[Nova Kakhovka airstrike]]
*****A massive explosion occurs in the city of [[Nova Kakhovka]] after [[Ukrainian forces]] destroy a Russian [[arms depot]]. Russian state news agency [[TASS]] claims that a market, hospital, and civilian housing were also damaged, and that multiple civilians were killed. Russian [[22nd Army Corps (Russian Federation)|22nd Army Corps]] general Artem Nasbulin is allegedly among the dead. [https://www.pravda.com.ua/news/2022/07/11/7357612/ (''Ukrayinska Pravda'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-prepares-fresh-russian-assault-west-braces-worsening-energy-crisis-2022-07-12/ (Reuters)] [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2022/07/12/ukraine-russia-war-kherson-attack-general-killed/8551657623145/ (UPI)]
***[[National Security Advisor (United States)|U.S. National Security Advisor]] [[Jake Sullivan]] claims that [[Iran]] will provide [[Russia]] with hundreds of drones along with the necessary training for their use. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2022/07/11/iran-drones-russia-ukraine/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[War crimes in Afghanistan]]
***Leaked military reports indicate that a United Kingdom [[Special Air Service]] (SAS) unit [[unlawfully killed]] at least 54 people during a six-month tour. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-62083196 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/7/12/bbc-probe-suggests-afghanistan-war-crimes-by-uk-special-forces (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War against the Islamic State]]
**The [[United States]] confirms that it has killed the leader of the [[Islamic State]]'s Syrian branch, Maher al-Agal, in a [[drone strike]] in northwestern [[Syria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/isis-leader-syria-killed-us-strike-us-officials-say-2022-07-12/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021–2022 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks]]
**Seven people are killed when suspected [[Islamist]]s attack the city of [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/suspected-islamists-kill-seven-east-congo-city-beni-2022-07-13/ (Reuters)] 

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Enlargement of the eurozone]]
**The [[European Union]] formally accepts [[Croatia]] as the 20th member of the [[Eurozone]]. Croatia will adopt the [[euro|bloc's currency]] on January 1, 2023. [https://www.cnbc.com/2022/07/12/eu-formally-accepts-croatia-as-20th-euro-zone-member.html (CNBC)]
*[[Proposed acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk]]
** [[Twitter]] sues [[Elon Musk]] in the [[Delaware Court of Chancery]], requesting the court to order Musk to proceed with the purchase of Twitter under the previously agreed upon terms. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-62144776 (BBC News)]
*[[Ukraine]] says that despite the Russian blockade of many of its [[Black Sea]] ports, in the last four days, 16 ships carrying grain have passed through the Bystre rivermouth, an important mouth of the [[Danube river]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-ministry-ships-passing-through-danube-bystre-rivermouth-2022-07-12/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Twenty-three bodies are found near [[hot springs]] in [[Michoacán]], [[Mexico]]. [https://apnews.com/article/mexico-caribbean-climate-and-environment-9335a17bd2da2d7e640c25417fa6fd77 (AP)]
*A chartered boat capsizes in the [[Hudson River]] in [[New York City]], killing two people and injuring three others. Twelve others are rescued alive from the water. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/07/13/us/manhattan-boat-capsizes-two-dead/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2022 monkeypox outbreak]]
**[[2022 monkeypox outbreak in Europe]]
***[[Russia]] reports its first case of [[monkeypox]] in a man who travelled from [[Europe]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-registers-first-case-monkeypox-2022-07-12/ (Reuters)]
*[[Vanuatu]] declares a [[malaria]] outbreak in four of its [[Provinces of Vanuatu|provinces]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/470803/vanuatu-declares-malaria-outbreak-in-four-provinces (RNZ)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Telford child sexual exploitation scandal]]
**A three-year-long independent inquiry into [[child sexual exploitation]] finds that over 1,000 children in [[Telford]], [[Shropshire]], [[England]], were [[sexual exploitation|sexually exploited]] beginning in the 1980s. Teachers and youth workers were discouraged from reporting child sexual abuse and police were nervous that investigating the abusers would inflame racial tensions. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/over-1000-children-english-town-were-sexually-exploited-inquiry-finds-2022-07-12/ (Reuters)] [https://www.theguardian.com/society/2022/jul/12/over-1000-children-telford-sexually-exploited-inquiry-finds (''The Guardian'')]
*Protesters in [[Panama]] continue blocking streets and railways, mainly in [[Chiriquí Province|Chiriquí]] and [[Veraguas Province]]s, rejecting the concession by [[President of Panama|president]] [[Laurentino Cortizo]] of freezing fuel prices. [https://www.telemetro.com/nacionales/continuan-los-cierres-vias-diferentes-puntos-chiriqui-y-veraguas-n5737938 (TeleMetro)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Sri Lankan political crisis]]
**[[President of Sri Lanka|President]] [[Gotabaya Rajapaksa]] and his wife are prevented from fleeing the country to [[Dubai]] by airport staff at [[Bandaranaike International Airport]] amid [[2022 Sri Lankan protests|nationwide protests]]. G. Rajapaksa has not given his official resignation yet. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/07/12/asia/sri-lanka-crisis-gotabaya-rajapaksa-airport-intl/index.html (CNN)]
**Rajapaksa subsequently flees the country on a military aircraft to the [[Maldives]], formally ending his rule of [[Sri Lanka]]. His brother, former finance minister [[Basil Rajapaksa]], also flees the country. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-62132271 (BBC News)]
